title: Bloom Level Task Sorter
creator: Dan McCreary
subject: AI-Native Schools
description: Sort twelve classroom tasks into the six levels of the revised Bloom's Taxonomy, with a hint and a second try for each task.

learningObjectives: The learner will classify twelve classroom tasks into the six levels of the 2001 revised Bloom's Taxonomy, correctly placing at least ten of twelve on the first attempt.
prerequisites: The six levels of Bloom's Taxonomy and the meaning of higher-order thinking, from Chapter 1.

pedagogical.teachingStrategy: Classify, commit an answer, and read the reason
keyQuestions: What kind of thinking does this task ask for?
Does the verb alone decide the level?
commonMisconceptions: The verb alone decides the level
Harder or longer tasks are always at higher levels
assessmentOpportunities: Why are "explain why ice floats" and "compare two accounts" at different levels?

controls.name: Six level buttons
controls.description: Choose Remember, Understand, Apply, Analyze, Evaluate, or Create for the current task.

controls.name: Show definitions
controls.description: Shows or hides the one-line definition of each level.

controls.name: Next
controls.description: Moves to the next task after feedback.

controls.name: Previous missed and Next missed
controls.description: On the results screen, step through the tasks you missed.

controls.name: Play again
controls.description: Reshuffles the tasks for a practice run.
